tagline: Out under the oaks and home along the ocean.
intro: The loop starts in Ormond Beach, known as the birthplace of speed, because early motorists raced on its hard-packed sand before paved roads were common. From town it heads north under tree canopy along parts of North Beach Street, Old Dixie Highway and Walter Boardman Lane, past tidal creeks, marsh and scrub, and comes back down A1A beside a long stretch of undeveloped beach. It is 34 miles in all, a double loop.
Right whales migrate off this coast from December to April to bear their calves, and sea turtles nest on the beach from May to September.

moments.title: The Casements
moments.text: John D. Rockefeller wintered here above the Halifax River from 1918 and handed out dimes to neighbors and visitors. When Harvey Firestone made a good golf shot, he got one too.

moments.title: Tomoka State Park
moments.text: On the Tomoka River stood the Timucuan village of Nocoroco. The mound complex just south of it may have been occupied as early as 5000 B.C.

moments.title: Bulow Creek State Park
moments.text: Off Old Dixie Highway the Fairchild Oak has stood more than four centuries, in one of the largest stands of southern live oak left on Florida's east coast.
